source.method: Disassembly listings from capstone 5.0.7 over the pinned image and ghidra-cli 0.2.2 queries on Ghidra 12.1.4 were treated as leads. Every instruction sequence, table and string below is confirmed against the pinned bytes by tools/verify_scb_clip_classes.py --exe. The install census and invariants are recomputed by tools/verify_scb_clip_classes.py --install.

registry.boundary: The registry object is u32(u32(S+0x6c))+8 for the singleton S returned by 0x00a02360, the same object the published layout page names. The Rapture group of 0x00635760 also re-registers some keys in the registry of a second singleton returned by 0x00a65600 and in the Lay registry. Those groups were not followed.

fields.feeds: Negative: the clip calls its slot 18 with 1 and its slot 12 with 0 and returns. Otherwise the index is passed to slot 3 of the scheduler name object at +0x74, which fills a 16 byte name record.
Bit 2 is stored in a request byte, bit 6 in clip +0x44 and a request byte, and bit 7 selects the selector branches. Bits 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 are not read.

The value 0xff becomes the signed integer -1 and any other value becomes its signed byte value minus 1. The result reaches the request only when bit 7 of +0x14 is set and bit 6 is clear. With bit 6 set the request word is -1 when bit 7 is set and 0 otherwise. With both clear it is 0. A result of -1 also makes the clip call its slot 12 with 2.

outcomes.claim: The base registrar 0x00a4c2a0 inserts SetPosClip (factory 0x00a4db10), ShowHideClip (0x00a4db80), MotionClip (0x00a4dcd0), ClipSyncClip (0x0063c570) and LocalCameraClip (0x00a4d950) through 0x0063f710. Manager slot 3 at 0x00635760 calls it at 0x00635899 and then inserts the Rapture group. In that group RapturePhysicsLookAtClip (0x0063a5f0) is a new key. SetPosClip (0x0063bd90), ShowHideClip (0x0063bf40) and MotionClip (0x0063c180) are each preceded by a call to 0x0063f920 with a second copy of the key literal. Both groups address the registry object reached through the singleton returned by 0x00a02360.

Insertion keeps the earlier factory for an equal key, and the call to 0x0063f920 before each of the three Rapture re-registrations is read as erase by key. The registry then holds the Rapture factories for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip and MotionClip, and the base factories for ClipSyncClip and LocalCameraClip. The body of 0x0063f920 was not walked.

Each factory stores its object size when the size argument is nonnull. The sizes are 0x38 for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip and RapturePhysicsLookAtClip, 0x60 for MotionClip, 0x3c for ClipSyncClip and 0x120 for LocalCameraClip. Each constructor installs the primary vtable at +0 and a secondary table at +8. In every primary vtable slot 1 calls the base method 0x00a20f30, which stores state 1 at clip +0x1c. Slot 2 is the update method. Slot 29 returns a class-specific address relative to D. It is the record end for SetPosClip, ShowHideClip and MotionClip. It is not the record end for the other three classes, as listed per class.

Base accessors read s16(D+8) in slot 22, u8(D+0x0a) in slot 23, bits 0, 1 and 2 of u8(D+0x0b) in slots 25, 27 and 26, and s16(D+0x0c) in slot 20, beside the u8(D+2), u8(D+3) and u32(D+4) readers in slots 5, 6 and 7. Slot 8 jumps through slot 7 unless a class overrides it. MotionClip returns u32(D+0x18) and LocalCameraClip returns u32(D+0x10) plus clip +0x110. Base slots 3 and 4 store state 3 and state 4, and the update method moves state 1 to state 2.

RaptureSetPosClip slot 1 at 0x0082a080 resolves the actor record, casts its slot 23 result from IActor to CharaActor, and fetches three vectors from the object at clip +0x24 through its slots 12, 14 and 16. It replaces the x, y and z floats of the vectors with the floats at +0x10, +0x1c and +0x28 where the flag bytes at +0x34 to +0x36, +0x38 to +0x3a and +0x3c to +0x3e are nonzero. When the scheduler test 0x00a1c050 is true it calls slot 18 of the target object with the three vectors and the scheduler origin. It then calls CharaActor setter 0x0065e660 with vector A and 0x0065e690 with vector B. Both receive the inverse of bit 0 of u8(D+0x37). Vector C reaches only the slot 18 call. Bytes +0x3b and +0x3f are not read.

Vector A is a position, vector B is a rotation in radians and vector C is a scale. The 33,078 install records hold A components between -2824.9 and 3563.5, B components within plus or minus pi and C components between 0.1 and 8.0. When CharaActor slot 154 returns 0, the setter 0x0065e660 stores the vector it receives at CharaActor +0x11f0. The roles of the slot 12, 14 and 16 vectors and of 0x0065e690 were not traced beyond the argument flow.

RaptureShowHideClip slot 1 at 0x0082de70 requires the actor record's slot 23 result to cast from IActor to RaptureActor and a nonnull pointer at RaptureActor +0x9c. It calls slot 2 of that pointer with the RaptureActor and the boolean u8(D+0x10) == 1. Slot 1 reads no record field beyond the actor ordinal and this byte. All 21,581 install records are 0x14 bytes and hold 0 or 1 at +0x10.

RaptureMotionClip slot 1 at 0x0082f120 ends the clip at once when s32(D+0x10) is negative. Otherwise it passes the index to slot 3 of the scheduler name object at +0x74, which fills a 16 byte name record. When slot 7 of the actor record is false, its slot 23 result is null or the actor address plus 0x11b4 is zero, it calls slot 12 with 0 and returns. When the name record starts with c or e, has m, f or h second and has an underscore third, it calls slot 18 with 1 and then slot 12 with 0. In every other case it builds a motion request from u8(D+0x14) bits 2, 6 and 7, u8(D+0x15), s32(D+0x1c) and s32(D+0x20) divided by 10000, u16(D+0x24) divided by 100.0 and u8(D+0x26), and passes it to 0x007b9920 with ECX at actor +0x4c0. Bytes +0x16, +0x17, +0x27 and the word at +0x28 are not read by slots 1, 2 or 3.

The 16 byte record is a motion name and the request starts that motion on the actor. The words at +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20 are multiples of 10000 in all 22,085 install records, which fits integer units scaled by 10000. The u16 at +0x24 is 100 in 20,305 records, which fits a percent scale. Names that start with cm_, cf_, ch_, em_, ef_ or eh_ end the clip without starting a motion.

RapturePhysicsLookAtClip slot 1 at 0x00821b40 casts the actor record to CharaActor and runs two passes. Pass 0 runs when u8(D+0x15) is nonzero and pass 1 when u8(D+0x16) is nonzero. Each pass switches on u32(D+0x1c). Mode 0 reads the target actor ordinal s32(D+0x20) when u8(D+0x14) is nonzero, a node index at +0x24 and an offset vector at +0x28, and calls 0x0065e730. Mode 1 reads the floats at +0x20 and +0x24, multiplies them by pi and divides by 180.0, and calls 0x00662be0. Mode 2 reads the vector at +0x20 and calls 0x0065e7c0. Any other mode runs no branch. The float at +0x18 is the first float argument of the mode 1 and mode 2 calls, ahead of the angles or vector. The error branches at 0x00821fae, 0x00821fd9 and 0x00822004 log missing target, not IActor and not CharaActor texts.

Mode 1 carries two angles in degrees and mode 2 a point. In the install the 2,169 mode 1 records hold angles within plus or minus 90, and 130 mode 2 records hold coordinate-sized floats. Mode 0 targets another actor by ordinal. The meaning of the two passes and of the node index was not traced.

ClipSyncClip is registered by the base registrar only. Slot 1 at 0x00a100b0 sets the byte at clip +0x38 to 0 and calls its slot 12 with 1. Slot 2 at 0x00a10120 reads u16(D+0x10). Its low 15 bits are the count n of s16 clip indexes at +0x14. Each index goes through the scheduler clip lookup 0x00a1b790, which returns 0 outside the clip array. With bit 15 set the clip calls its slot 12 with 0 once every listed clip is in state 3 or 4. With bit 15 clear it does so as soon as one listed clip is. Slot 29 returns D + ((2n + 0x19) & ~3), which equals the record end (2n + 0x17) & ~3 for odd n and lies 4 bytes past it for even n.

LocalCameraClip is registered by the base registrar only. Slot 1 at 0x00a0c740 reads u8(D+3), u16(D+0x14), s16(D+0x0c), s16(D+8), s16(D+0x1c), u16(D+0x16) and u8(D+0x18), stores at clip +0x74 whether a scheduler lookup byte is nonzero, and pushes u16(D+0x16) and u8(D+0x18) as arguments of the virtual calls at 0x00a0ca27 and 0x00a0ca50. Every read of u8(D+0x1a) in slots 1 and 2 first loads the class key entry from clip +0x18 and skips the read when key entry byte +4 is below 4 (0x00a0ca52, 0x00a0c11e, 0x00a0c15d). When that byte is at least 4 and bit 0 of u8(D+0x1a) is set, slot 1 passes D+0x20 to 0x00a0b9c0, which reads a bind record of s16 actor ordinal, s16 part index, six floats and two bytes. Negative ordinals or part indexes take error branches. Bit 2 of u8(D+0x1a) is read by slot 2 under the same key entry gate. Slot 8 returns u32(D+0x10) plus clip +0x110. Slot 29 returns D+0x24, the first extension float, and the extension itself starts at D+0x20.

The scheduler resource loader at 0x00a24400 calls 0x00a27210 for the @CCPT chunk. For each four byte name entry it stores the address of the String table entry named by u16(entry) at key entry +0 and the byte at name entry +2 at key entry +4, in 8 byte key entries. The clip builder 0x00a28510 selects keyEntry = table + 8 * u8(D+2) and hands it to the factory, whose constructor stores it at clip +0x18.

The table the clip builder reads at +0x0c of its owner is the table 0x00a27210 fills, because both use 8 byte entries with the string pointer at +0 and the entry is passed on as the class key. The owner object that holds the table was not traced. The role of the @CCPT entry byte +2, which equals 4 for LocalCameraClip in all 663 schedulers that list it, is UNKNOWN beyond this gate.
The object at RaptureActor +0x9c, whose slot 2 receives the ShowHideClip operand, was not identified. RaptureActor's constructor at 0x007ced70 does not store it.

The shared header words s16(D+8), u8(D+0x0a), u8(D+0x0b) and s16(D+0x0c) are read by accessors whose callers were not traced. The fields of the four classes listed in the manifest are only the ones read by slot 1 and by the slot 2 and slot 8 methods named above. The second-group registrations and the Lay registry were not followed.

The scan reads 9,593 files below client/cut, finds 86,405 SEDB headers of which 689 fold to scb, and parses every scheduler. The 222,491 clip records use 102 classes. The six classes in this manifest are ranks 1 to 6 and hold 120,252 records. The full ranking is in cut-scheduler-clip-class-census.csv.

The invariants listed in the manifest hold for every record of their class: record sizes, flag bytes and enumerations, padding words, the ClipSyncClip index range, the LocalCameraClip extension, the SetPosClip rotation range, the MotionClip scaled words and the PhysicsLookAtClip mode 1 angle range and the @CCPT entry byte +2 of each class. The install section also pins the ShowHideClip operand, MotionClip speed, PhysicsLookAtClip mode and ClipSyncClip count parity distributions and the SetPosClip position and scale ranges.
